newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on Yeltsin, wary of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on Yeltsin, wary of U.S. data.

text.p: MinFin bonds, wary ahead of Friday's U.S. statistics data, corrected downward in active trading on Thursday, but they were higher than Wednesday's levels on a lively speech by President Boris Yeltsin.
MinFin bonds, like Brady debt, are heavily influenced by moves in the U.S. Treasury bond market.
Yeltsin, making his annual state-of-the-nation address to parliament, said he would announce a government shake-up soon and said the economy was still in crisis.
"Prices rose in the morning as Yeltsin's address was lively and active. Then prices eased as somebody decided to take profits," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
He said that trading activity was brisk, with banks striking direct deals, an unusual phenomenon for the market.
Dealers said the 2003 and 2008 maturities were traded the most, with prices fluctuating in the ranges of 63.00-63.30 to 63.60-63.90 and 44.10-44.40 to 44.50-44.80, respectively.

A Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said stronger U.S. Treasuries were another encouraging factor, but wariness was seen on the market ahead of United States payroll and unemployment data due on Friday at 1330 GMT.

"MinFins seem quite strong, since Yeltsin put in a good performance and U.S. Treasuries recovered," he said. "But people are not certain prices will hold at these levels and the market is very volatile and depending on U.S. figures."
